headline: Trump asked the UFC boss to be his press secretary.
summary: Trump posted Saturday from his Florida golf club that he has offered Dana White, his friend and the head of UFC, the job of White House press secretary. Nobody at the White House confirmed it. The job has been empty since Katie Zacharia left after five days in October. White posted a photo of himself behind the briefing-room podium.

cover_question.q: What does a press secretary do?

cover_answer: Speaks for the president. Trump has nobody doing it.
table_question: Would you offer a friend a big job in public before asking them first?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president wants a new helper whose job is to stand at a podium and answer reporters' questions. He asked Dana White, who runs the cage-fighting league UFC, and he did it in a post for everyone to read. It's like picking the team captain by shouting it across the playground. Nobody is hurt, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: One picture stands in for the event at seven, so make it the podium. A kid this age can't weigh a job offer yet, but can see a shout across a playground.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old reasons from what is in front of them and takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script hands them a podium and a shout across the playground and leaves the politics out. Expect "did he say yes?" Not yet. He put up a photo of himself at the podium, and he is meeting the president on Monday.

8-12.script: Republicans lost Congress on Tuesday. By Friday Trump had swapped his chief of staff. On Saturday he posted that he wants Dana White, the UFC boss, as press secretary, with fighters as "assistants." The White House didn't confirm it. Like a coach who loses big and switches players that week.
8-12.why: Loss, shake-up, surprise pick is a chain they can follow at nine.
8-12.why_long: A nine-year-old is working out cause and effect and whether adults follow their own rules, so the script runs the chain in order: the loss Tuesday, the chief of staff swapped Friday, the post Saturday, a White House that would not confirm it. The coach switching players is the mechanism. Expect "is he serious?" Nobody knows yet.

13-17.script: Should the president's spokesperson be someone who spent years fighting with reporters? Dana White runs UFC, once put out a video attacking journalists, and Trump asked him in a post, with six fighters as "assistants." Second: the White House wouldn't confirm it. Is an offer nobody confirms real, or a show?
13-17.why: Trump wrote it and his staff won't confirm it. At 14 they can hold both as true.
13-17.why_long: A 14-year-old can hold two true things at once, so the script gives both: the president wrote the offer, and his own staff would not confirm it. The second question asks them to decide what an unconfirmed offer is, which is the practice. Expect "why him?" They are close friends, and White credits Trump with saving UFC in 2001.

5-7.q: What does a press secretary do?
5-7.a: Answers reporters' questions for the president, from a podium.

8-12.a: Nobody knows. The White House didn't answer. They meet Monday.

8-12.q: Can fighters really be his assistants?
8-12.a: Trump asked for six. Nobody has said what they'd do, or said yes.

13-17.q: Does he know anything about the job?
13-17.a: He runs UFC and spoke at three Republican conventions. Not press work.

13-17.q: Why would Trump pick a fight promoter?
13-17.a: Close friends. White credits Trump with saving UFC in 2001.
